title: Change one thing per ablation, and what a mixture weight changes
design_ref: What each choice changes; SFT: data mixtures and loss masking
purpose: The launcher must refuse an ablation whose diff touches more than its declared variable, and create nothing. A correct one-key ablation (more reasoning traces in the mixture) runs on the ablation queue and is compared with its parent on the same suites.

checks.description: an ablation that changes two keys is refused, and names the undeclared one
checks.because: The launcher diffs the flattened recipe against its parent and compares the changed keys with the declared variable.

checks.description: nothing was created: no Job, no run record
checks.because: The check runs before anything is written to S3 or sent to the API server.

checks.description: the one-key ablation was accepted and runs on the ablation queue at low priority
checks.because: For an ablation the launcher always uses the ablation queue and priority class, whatever the recipe says.

checks.description: the ablation's record names its parent, the variable and both values; its mixture really is reasoning-heavy
checks.because: Weight 1.5 among 0.45, 0.15 and 0.15 normalises to 0.667, and 1,600 examples are drawn either way, so only the mixture differs.

checks.description: both models were scored by the same suites, so the difference is attributable to the one key
checks.because: Same eval recipe, same datasets (by hash), greedy decoding.

checks.description: more reasoning traces made casual answers come out in numbered steps more often, and lowered the house-style rate
checks.because: Quick conversion questions of families that neither source covers are answered in whichever style dominates the mixture.

checks.description: the gate blocked the ablation on behaviour, with its reasons in the registry
checks.because: A candidate must pass every gate, not improve on average: a capability gain does not buy a behaviour regression.

notes: Gate verdict for the reasoning-heavy SFT: blocked.
